_note: DRAFT writing for The Wyrd Reading Together (two to nine people), for The Völva to rewrite. Placeholders in curly braces are filled in by the site; keep them. Change any line and every reading changes with it. The free Compare writing lives in static/dynamics.js; this is the paid side, built around timing.
OPENING: This reading is for the people at one table: who sent each of you, what each of you wakes in the others, and the seasons you share. Read the story first. The rest decodes it.
CLOSING: A bond is a set of engines too, and it has its seasons. Work the questions together, out loud if you can.
PROLOGUE_SUB: a silly story of how you ended up together
PROLOGUE_OPEN: Long before you met, each of you stood in the queue at the Well of Urðr, on different days, with no idea the others existed. Urðr, who keeps what has already happened, looked each of you up in her book.
PROLOGUE_PERSON: {name} had been sent by {sent}, and chose {wore}.
PROLOGUE_TABLE_TWO: What neither of you knew was that Skuld, who keeps what shall be, had already put the two of you at the same table. She does this on purpose. She says it saves time.
PROLOGUE_TABLE_MANY: What none of you knew was that Skuld, who keeps what shall be, had already put all {n} of you at the same table. She does this on purpose. She says it saves time, and that the arguments are good for everyone.
PROLOGUE_NOW: She checked the appointment books, as she does. Right now, {guests}. {season}
PROLOGUE_CLOSE: That is the story. Who Sits at the Table decodes who sent you. The Bond decodes why Skuld bothered. What You Wake in Each Other decodes why it felt like that from the start. The Old Match, How Your Bodies Meet and Your Numbers Together decode the gifts. The Seasons You Share decodes the appointment book.

TABLE_SUB: each of you: who sent you, the costume, and the guest staying now
TABLE_INTRO: Each person's soul-planet is the planet furthest through its sign: the one that sent them, and the one that holds the errand. The seat is the rising sign. The guest is the planet whose period is running in that life now.
BOND_SUB: what it is for, its higher and lower paths, and every contact in words
BOND_INTRO: The bond by the lunar mansions (Sukuyō), and by the planets between you: what it is for, how it lifts you, how it drags, and how to weave the two.
WAKE_TITLE: What You Wake in Each Other
WAKE_SUB: where each of you lands in the other's life
WAKE_INTRO: Lay one chart over another and every planet of one person falls in a house of the other's. Two matter most here: the soul-planet, which is what you were sent to do, and the guest staying with you now, which is what you are busy with. Where they land in another person's chart is the part of their life you stir up, whether either of you meant to.
WAKE_SOUL: {a}'s soul-planet, {planet}, lands in {b}'s {house} house: {life}. {a} brings {lends} there, for good.
WAKE_GUEST: For now, {a}'s guest, {lord}, stands in {b}'s {house} house: while it stays, {a} stirs up {b}'s {life}.
UNKNOWN_HOUSES: {name}'s birth time is unknown, so {name}'s houses are counted from the Sun's sign.
SEASON_SUB: the next thirty years, chapter by chapter
SEASON_INTRO: Every life is a house with one planet in residence at a time, staying for years, and each long stay is divided into nine shorter ones. When two people share their days, their guests share them too, and how those planets get on sets the weather between you. The tradition keeps a table of which planets are friends, which are neutral and which are enemies; Rahu is read like Saturn and Ketu like Mars. Above the houses the slow planets keep their own appointments: the returns of Saturn, Jupiter and the nodes, and Saturn's long crossing of the Moon. This section walks the next thirty years chapter by chapter, then lays them out year by year.

same.label: the same planet
same.text: The same planet is running both your lives at once. You want the same things at the same time, which is wonderful until you both want the last biscuit.

allies.label: allies
allies.text: Your two guests are old friends. They lend each other tools and make the season between you easy. Use it to build.

friendly.label: warm on one side
friendly.text: One guest likes the other more than it is liked back. The season is warm on one side; the warmer one should say so, and the other should notice.

polite.label: polite strangers
polite.text: Your two guests are polite strangers. Nothing between you is blocked and nothing is pushed: whatever this season becomes, you make it.

uneasy.label: uneasy
uneasy.text: Your two guests don't quite trust each other, and small things rub. It is a season for saying the small thing early, before it grows teeth.

odds.label: at odds
odds.text: Your two guests are at odds. The season tests the bond, and the test is the point: what survives it is load-bearing.

ASKS_SUB: for the table, in the order the reading asked them
ASKS: What were each of you sent to do, and does the other know?
Where does the other land in your life, and have you ever said so out loud?
What is this season asking you to build together, and what is it asking you to stop expecting?
When the next guest arrives, what will you want to have already said?
PROLOGUE_GIFTS: Verðandi packed each of you a gift, with its shadow folded into the same bag: {gifts}. Neither of you has found the shadow yet. You will find each other's first.
PROLOGUE_BOOK: Skuld's appointment book was already full. {turn} {mark} She underlined {year} twice and would not say why.
PROLOGUE_TURN: The next guest due is {lord}, for {name}, in {year}.
PROLOGUE_ERRAND: On the last page, under both your names, she wrote what the table is for: {errand}
PROLOGUE_ERRAND_PLAIN: to grow each other on purpose, and to say so out loud.
CHAPTER_OPEN: From {from} to {to}, {la} stays with {a} and {lb} stays with {b}. The two guests are {label}.
CHAPTER_LANDS: {a}'s {lord} stands in {b}'s {house} house: through these years {a} stirs up {b}'s {life}.
SUB_LINE: {name}'s {lord} sub-period begins: {short}. The two shorter guests are {label}.

LORD_BOND.Sun: The Sun's years make {name} want to be seen, by the world and by the people closest. The bond does well when it admires out loud, and badly when it competes for the light.
LORD_BOND.Moon: The Moon's years turn {name} toward home, feeling and family. Expect more moods and more need; this is when a bond's comfort is built, or found missing.
LORD_BOND.Mars: Mars's years give {name} drive, heat and the need for a project. Give the fire a job, or it will find one inside the bond.
LORD_BOND.Mercury: Mercury's years make {name} talk, trade, study and plan. The bond lives in conversation now: keep the talk honest and the lists shared.
LORD_BOND.Jupiter: Jupiter's years bring {name} growth, teachers, faith and luck, sometimes children. The bond expands; watch that it does not promise more than it can keep.
LORD_BOND.Venus: Venus's years bring {name} pleasure, beauty, love and money. The bond can bloom here, or be tested by someone or something lovely.
LORD_BOND.Saturn: Saturn's years ask {name} for work, weight and patience. The bond is tested by duty, and whatever survives is built in stone.
LORD_BOND.Rahu: Rahu's years make {name} hungry: for more, for new, for whatever was forbidden. Ambition or restlessness runs high; name the hunger before it names itself.
LORD_BOND.Ketu: Ketu's years pull {name} inward, toward letting go and the spiritual. {name} may seem far away; the bond needs room here, not chasing.

SUB_SHORT.Saturn: a season of work and weight
SUB_SHORT.Rahu: a season of hunger and sudden change

MARKS.saturn_return: {name}'s Saturn return, {when}: Saturn comes back to where it stood at {name}'s birth, and the life is audited. What was built on sand comes down. For the bond, a time to recommit on purpose, or to stop pretending.
MARKS.saturn_opposition: {name}'s Saturn opposition, {when}: Saturn halfway round, the midlife reckoning. The bond is asked whether it still fits the person {name} is becoming.
MARKS.jupiter_return: {name}'s Jupiter return, {when}: Jupiter comes home. A year of growth and fresh faith, and a good year to begin something together.
MARKS.nodal_return: {name}'s nodal return, {when}: the nodes come round to where they stood at birth. A turn of direction: what {name} hungers for resets.
MARKS.sade_sati: {name}'s Sade Sati, {when}: Saturn crosses the three signs around {name}'s Moon, seven and a half years of pressure on the heart and the home. Carry each other's load here; it is the long test.

MARK_SHORT.sade_sati: Saturn begins its long crossing of {name}'s Moon

YEARS_INTRO: The same thirty years at a glance: each person's long guest and shorter guest in the middle of the year, how the long guests get on, and the sky's appointments. Marked years are the ones to watch: both of you change at once, or the sky's appointments pile up.
WATCH_NONE: No year piles up: the changes come one at a time.
NUM_SUB: life paths and names, side by side
NUM_INTRO: Each of you carries numbers from your birth date and, if it was given, your full name at birth. Here they sit side by side. Each number sits on two planets, the console's own Stavefall seat and the Vedic one, and how those planets get on is how the two numbers get on. How the numbers work →
NUM_PAIR_SAME: You share the number: the same road, walked side by side. Recognition is easy, and so are shared blind spots.
NUM_PAIR: By Stavefall the planets beneath them, {sa} and {sb}, are {ls}; by the Vedic seating, {va} and {vb}, they are {lv}.

NUM_MEANING.same: the numbers stand on the same ground
NUM_MEANING.allies: the numbers pull the same way
NUM_MEANING.friendly: one number warms to the other more than it is warmed
NUM_MEANING.polite: the numbers leave each other room
NUM_MEANING.uneasy: the numbers rub: say what each one needs
NUM_MEANING.odds: the numbers pull opposite ways, and the friction is the work

NUM_NO_NAME: Name numbers appear for everyone whose full name at birth was given.
KUTA_SUB: Ashtakoota, the eight-fold Jyotish match, in words
KUTA_INTRO: Jyotish matches two people by their Moons: the sign and the birth star each was born under. Eight measures add up to 36 points. Tradition reads the match in a fixed order, one partner first; three of the measures change with that order, so this reading counts it both ways. A score is a starting point, not a verdict.

KUTA_VERDICT.strong: a strong match by the old count
KUTA_VERDICT.workable: a workable match by the old count
KUTA_VERDICT.demanding: a demanding match by the old count: the bond asks for conscious work

Varna.full: Your temperaments sit comfortably: neither has to strain to respect the other.
Varna.none: Your spiritual footings differ: respect has to be chosen rather than assumed.

Vashya.full: The pull runs both ways: each of you draws the other.
Vashya.part: One of you draws the other more; the pull is real, but uneven.
Vashya.none: Neither of you naturally sways the other; attraction here is built rather than given.

Tara.full: Each birth star is kind to the other: the stars wish you well.
Tara.part: One star is kind and one is testing: luck favours the bond from one side.
Tara.none: Both stars count as testing: the bond makes its own luck.

Yoni.about: instinct and intimacy, read through the animal of each birth star
Yoni.full: Your instincts match: the animals of your birth stars are at ease together, and closeness comes naturally.
Yoni.part: Your instincts are different animals that can learn each other; intimacy takes patience.
Yoni.none: Your birth-star animals are old enemies: instinct needs translating, and tenderness has to be deliberate.

Graha Maitri.about: the friendship of the two Moon-sign lords: how your minds get on
Graha Maitri.full: Your Moon-sign lords are friends: your minds get on.
Graha Maitri.part: Your minds are civil rather than close; you understand each other by effort.
Graha Maitri.none: Your Moon-sign lords are at odds: you think differently, and arguments need rules.

Gana.part: One nature is gentler than the other; the fiercer has to learn restraint.
Gana.none: Your natures clash; the bond needs agreed limits.

Bhakoot.about: the distance between your Moon signs: love, money and the life you build
Bhakoot.full: Your Moon signs sit at an easy distance for love, money and the life you build.
Bhakoot.none: Your Moon signs sit at a testing distance (2–12, 5–9 or 6–8): be explicit about money and family.

Nadi.full: Your pulses differ, and balance each other.
Nadi.none: You share a Nadi, the same bodily pulse: the tradition's most serious single mismatch. Living closely, you can wear out each other's constitution; give each other rest and room.

HD_SUB: your two designs, side by side, in words
HD_INTRO: Lay one bodygraph over another and some channels light up only when you are together, some you share, and some one of you carries for both. Where one of you is defined and the other open, the open one feels the defined one's energy amplified, and can mistake it for their own.
HD_TYPES: {a} is a {ta} with {aa} authority; {b} is a {tb} with {ab} authority. Together your two bodies make one field: a {tc}.

HD_KIND.em: Electromagnetic: each of you holds one end of the channel, and together it lights up. This is the spark between you, and the place you most easily rub.
HD_KIND.comp: Companionship: you both carry the channel whole. Here you understand each other without effort, and share one way of being.
HD_KIND.dom: Dominance: one of you carries the whole channel and the other has neither gate. Here one leads and the other learns the current from outside.
HD_KIND.promise: Compromise: one of you carries the whole channel and the other only one of its gates. The one with the whole current tends to win here; the other gives way, and should notice when that costs too much.

HD_COND: {a}'s defined {centre} ({does}) is amplified in {b}, whose {centre} is open. For {b}: {open}
HD_COND_NONE: You are defined and open in the same centres, so little amplification passes between you.
HD_OPEN_BOTH: Open in both of you: {centres}. Here the two of you take in the world together; other people and places will colour these centres for you both.
